en: to be unmanageable; to be too much for

examples.en: There's too much work these days and it's overwhelming.
Carrying the heavy luggage alone was too much for me.

examples.ko: 이 상대는 저에게 조금 버거운 것 같아요.
examples.en: This opponent seems a little too tough for me.

examples.ko: 버거운 일이 있으면 혼자 끙끙대지 마세요.
examples.en: If something is too much for you, don't struggle alone.
The rent got harder and harder to bear, so I decided to move.

examples.ko: 아이 둘을 키우는 게 가끔 버거울 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes raising two kids is too much.

explain: '버겁다'는 힘이나 능력보다 일이 더 커서 감당하기 어렵다는 느낌이에요. '힘들다'는 고생스러운 것 전체를 말하고, '버겁다'는 내 한계를 넘는다는 점이 달라요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '버거워요', '버거운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: It's a task that is too much to do alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '버거운'으로 바뀌어 감당하기 어려운 일을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to 버거운 before a noun to describe something hard to handle.

phrases.example: 이 정도 양은 저한테 버겁지 않아요.
phrases.en: This amount isn't too much for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 내가 충분히 할 수 있다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you can handle it fine.

phrases.en: You look like you're struggling with so many bags.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 힘들어하는 모습을 보고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you see someone else struggling.

explain_en: 버겁다 has the feeling that something is bigger than your strength or ability. 힘들다 covers any hardship, while 버겁다 stresses that it goes beyond your limit. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes 버거워요 and 버거운.

examples.en: My heart swelled with emotion on graduation day.

examples.ko: 합격 소식을 듣고 감동이 벅차올라서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Hearing I had passed, I was so overcome with emotion that I cried.
Hearing the cheering, joy wells up inside me.

examples.ko: 가슴이 벅차오르는 순간을 오래 기억하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to remember this moment when my heart swells for a long time.

examples.ko: 아이의 첫걸음을 보고 가슴이 벅차오를 만큼 행복했어요.
examples.en: Seeing my child's first steps, I was so happy my heart overflowed.

examples.ko: 이 노래를 들으면 알 수 없는 감정이 벅차올라요.
examples.en: When I hear this song, a feeling I can't name wells up in me.

explain: '가슴이/마음이 벅차오르다'처럼 주로 기쁨이나 감동 같은 좋은 감정에 써요. '오르다'처럼 '올라요, 올랐어요'로 바뀌는 르 불규칙이에요. '북받치다'는 슬픔이나 화처럼 눌렀던 감정이 터질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I was speechless from the overwhelming emotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 감정을 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-는' to describe the emotion that follows.

phrases.en: Hearing the cheers, my heart swelled with emotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가슴' 대신 '마음'을 쓰면 감정이 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using '마음' instead of '가슴' sounds a bit softer.

phrases.en: Seeing my child's first steps fills my heart with joy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 느끼는 감정을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in polite speech for a feeling you have right now.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '가슴이/마음이 벅차오르다' for good feelings such as joy and being moved. It follows the 르 irregular pattern like '오르다': 올라요, 올랐어요. '북받치다' can also be used for pent-up feelings such as sadness or anger bursting out.

en: to be dumbfounded; to be bemused

examples.en: I was dumbfounded by the sudden news.

examples.ko: 무슨 말인지 몰라서 한참 벙벙해 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't understand what was said and stood there bewildered for a while.
My friend suddenly started crying and I was dumbstruck too.
I'm in a daze at the news that I won the lottery.

examples.ko: 벙벙한 표정으로 서 있는 그에게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: I explained things to him as he stood there looking bewildered.

examples.ko: 너무 놀라서 한동안 벙벙하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked that I stood there dazed for a while.

explain: 거의 '어안이 벙벙하다'로 써요. 갑자기 놀라거나 어이가 없어서 말이 안 나오고 멍한 상태예요. '당황하다'는 허둥대는 느낌이 있고, '벙벙하다'는 멍하니 굳은 느낌에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 시험에 합격했다는 말을 듣고 어안이 벙벙했어요.
phrases.en: I was dumbfounded when I heard I had passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻밖의 일에 놀라 말문이 막힌 상태를 나타내는 굳은 표현이에요. 좋은 일과 나쁜 일 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set expression for being struck speechless by something unexpected. It can be used for both good and bad news.

explain_en: It is almost always used in '어안이 벙벙하다'. It describes being so surprised or taken aback that you cannot speak and feel dazed. '당황하다' suggests flustered flailing, while '벙벙하다' is closer to being frozen in a blank daze.

examples.en: Hearing my mom's voice makes my sorrow well up.
Grief welled up so much that I couldn't go on speaking.
Joy surged up inside me at the news that I passed.
I couldn't hold back the tears welling up.
My anger surged up and I shouted.

examples.ko: 분노가 복받칠 때는 잠깐 밖에 나가요.
examples.en: When anger wells up, I step outside for a moment.

explain: 설움, 눈물, 분노, 기쁨 같은 감정이 속에서 세게 치밀어 오를 때 써요. '감정이 복받치다' 형태로 쓰고, 감정이 아닌 물건에는 쓰지 않아요. 활용은 '복받쳐요', '복받친' 이에요.

phrases.en: Tears welled up as I read the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물, 설움 같은 감정과 자주 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with feelings such as tears or sorrow.

phrases.en: Anger surged up inside me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복받쳐 오르다'는 감정이 점점 치미는 모습을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes feelings rising up more and more.

phrases.en: I barely held back my overwhelming emotions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 명사를 꾸며요. 참기 힘든 감정이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies a noun, giving a sense of emotions hard to hold back.

explain_en: Use it when strong feelings such as sorrow, tears, anger or joy rise up from inside. It is used in the pattern 'emotion + 복받치다' and not for physical objects. The forms are '복받쳐요' and '복받친'.

examples.en: I was furious when I heard the lie.

examples.ko: 분통을 참느라 한참 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak for a while because I was holding in my anger.
This is really infuriating.
When I hear that story, my anger surges.
It's no use blowing up in anger.
After waiting and waiting, only my frustration piled up.

explain: 억울하고 분해서 화가 치미는 마음을 말해요. 거의 '분통이 터지다'로 쓰고, '분통을 터뜨리다'는 그 화를 밖으로 드러낸다는 뜻이에요. '화'보다 억울함이 섞인 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 버스가 또 안 와서 분통이 터져요.
phrases.en: The bus didn't come again and I'm fuming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억울하거나 답답한 일 때문에 화를 참기 힘들 때 써요. 화가 안에서 터져 나온다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can hardly hold back anger caused by something unfair or frustrating. It is a figure of speech about anger bursting out.

explain_en: It describes the angry feeling that surges when you feel wronged or resentful. It almost always appears as '분통이 터지다', and '분통을 터뜨리다' means to let that anger out. Compared with plain '화', it carries more of a sense of unfairness.

examples.en: I flared up over a small thing and shouted.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 나도 모르게 불끈했어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, I flared up before I knew it.
When his younger brother teased him, the older brother flared up and stood.

examples.ko: 불끈하는 성격 때문에 손해를 많이 봐요.
examples.en: I lose out a lot because of my hot-tempered personality.
Don't flare up so much; let's talk calmly.
My friend flared up and stormed out of the room.

explain: 갑자기 화나 감정이 확 치밀 때 써요. '발끈하다'가 비슷한 말이고, 둘 다 순간적으로 화를 내는 모습이에요. 부사 '불끈'과 함께 '화가 불끈 나다'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 말에 발끈해서 큰 소리로 대답했어요.
phrases.en: I flared up at those words and answered loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불끈하다'와 비슷하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 불끈하다 and used more often in daily life.

phrases.en: My friend suddenly burst out in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 소리 지르며 화낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gets angry with a loud shout.

phrases.en: I suddenly got angry and hung up the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불끈하다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to explain 불끈하다 in plain words.

explain_en: It is used when anger or emotion suddenly rushes up. '발끈하다' is a similar word, and both describe flaring up in the moment. You can also use the adverb, as in '화가 불끈 나다'.

en: to pierce the heart, to be deeply felt

examples.ko: 고향을 떠나 보니 부모님 생각이 사무쳤다.
examples.en: After leaving home, I missed my parents terribly.

examples.ko: 명절이 되면 돌아가신 할머니가 사무치게 그리워요.
examples.en: On holidays, I miss my late grandmother so much it hurts.

examples.ko: 고향을 떠난 지 십 년이 됐지만 집밥이 사무치게 그리워요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since I left home, but I still long deeply for home cooking.

examples.ko: 그 말 한마디가 가슴에 사무쳐서 오래 잊을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: That one remark sank deep into my heart and I couldn't forget it for a long time.

examples.ko: 타국에서 혼자 맞는 명절에는 외로움이 사무쳐요.
examples.en: Spending a holiday alone in a foreign country, the loneliness cuts deep.

explain: 사무치다는 감정이 가슴 깊이 스며드는 느낌이에요. 그리움, 외로움, 원망 같은 깊은 감정과 어울려요. 말보다 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 고향에 대한 사무치는 그리움을 편지에 썼어요.
phrases.en: I wrote my deep longing for my hometown in a letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '사무치는'으로 써요. 매우 깊은 그리움을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes 사무치는, showing very deep longing.

phrases.en: Spending winter alone, the loneliness sinks deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외로움이 가슴 깊이 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when loneliness is felt deep in the heart.

phrases.en: That one sentence still pierces my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말이나 일이 오래 마음에 남을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a word or event stays deep in your heart for a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to cut deep into the heart

dict_examples.en: I love you with a love that reaches the heavens.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 오래 떠나 있던 고향이 사무치게 그리워졌다.
dict_examples.en: I came to miss my hometown, which I had been away from for so long, deeply.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 사무치다 describes a feeling soaking deep into the heart. It goes with deep emotions like longing, loneliness and resentment, and shows up more in writing and song lyrics than in everyday speech.

examples.ko: 친구가 떠난 뒤 큰 상실감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a deep sense of loss after my friend left.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 일하던 회사를 나오니 상실감이 컸어요.
examples.en: Leaving the company I'd worked at for years left me with a big sense of loss.

examples.ko: 상실감 때문에 아무것도 하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of this sense of loss, I don't want to do anything.
He went on a trip to soothe his sense of loss.

examples.ko: 이사하고 나서 이유 없는 상실감이 몰려왔어요.
examples.en: After I moved, a sense of loss came over me for no reason.
I comforted my friend who was sunk in a sense of loss.

explain: 물건보다 사람, 꿈, 자리처럼 마음에 큰 것을 잃었을 때 써요. '상실감을 느끼다/겪다', '상실감이 크다'로 말해요. 가벼운 물건을 잃었을 때는 '아쉽다', '허전하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '-감'은 느낌을 뜻해서 '안도감', '성취감'과 같은 틀이에요.

phrases.example: 오랜 친구와 멀어진 뒤 큰 상실감에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: I fell into a deep sense of loss after drifting from an old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 상실감 때문에 힘들어하는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being overwhelmed by a deep sense of loss.
phrases.en_equiv: sink into a sense of loss

phrases.en: I went through a sense of loss after the breakup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 감정을 한동안 경험했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you experienced that feeling for a while.
phrases.en_equiv: go through a sense of loss

phrases.en: My friend moved away, so I feel empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상실감보다 가벼운 느낌이고, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter feeling than 상실감, used more often in daily talk.

explain_en: It is used when you lose something big to the heart, such as a person, a dream or a position, more than an object. You say '상실감을 느끼다/겪다' and '상실감이 크다'. For losing something small, '아쉽다' or '허전하다' is more natural. '-감' means a feeling, as in '안도감' and '성취감'.

examples.en: After the accident he lost his memory.

examples.ko: 한 번 실패했다고 자신감을 상실하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't lose your confidence just because you failed once.

examples.ko: 그 일로 많은 사람이 일자리를 상실했어요.
examples.en: Many people lost their jobs because of that.

examples.ko: 의욕을 상실한 사람에게는 쉬는 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: Someone who has lost motivation needs time to rest.

examples.ko: 이 제도는 시간이 지나면서 의미를 상실해요.
examples.en: This system loses its meaning as time passes.

examples.ko: 한번 신뢰를 상실하면 다시 얻기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once you lose trust, it is hard to get it back.

explain: '잃다/잃어버리다'가 일상 말이라면 '상실하다'는 기억, 자신감, 자격, 의욕처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것을 잃을 때 쓰는 글말이에요. 지갑이나 우산 같은 물건에는 '잃어버리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: If you break the rules, you lose your eligibility as a player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리나 자격을 잃을 때 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression for losing a right or qualification.

phrases.en: These days I've lost my motivation for work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 마음이 없어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the desire to do something has disappeared.

phrases.en: He lost his memory in an accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요. '상실하다'는 글에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easier everyday word; 상실하다 is more of a written word.

explain_en: 잃다/잃어버리다 are the everyday words, while 상실하다 is a written word for losing things you cannot see, such as memory, confidence, qualifications, or motivation. For objects like a wallet or umbrella, use 잃어버리다.

en: to avenge; to revenge; to get even

examples.ko: 이번 경기에서 꼭 지난 패배를 설욕하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to make up for our last defeat in this game.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 결승에서 작년의 패배를 설욕했어요.
examples.en: That player avenged last year's loss in the final.
The chance to get even has finally come to us.

examples.ko: 지난번에 진 팀을 이겨서 설욕하는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: We beat the team that beat us last time, so we got our revenge.

examples.ko: 어떻게든 설욕해야 마음이 편할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I'll only feel at ease if I get even somehow.

examples.ko: 그는 설욕하려고 일 년 동안 열심히 훈련했어요.
examples.en: He trained hard for a year in order to win back his honor.

explain: '복수하다'는 상대를 앙갚음한다는 느낌이 강하지만, '설욕하다'는 졌던 경기나 대결에서 이겨서 명예를 되찾는다는 느낌이에요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '패배를 설욕하다'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The chance to get even has finally come.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 기회'를 붙여서 다시 겨룰 기회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄹ 기회 talks about a chance to compete again.

phrases.example: 지난 패배를 설욕하기 위해 매일 연습했어요.
phrases.en: I practiced every day to make up for the past defeat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표를 말할 때 '-기 위해'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used with -기 위해 to state a goal.

phrases.en: He said he would definitely get even next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다짐을 전하는 말로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can be used to convey a determined promise.

explain_en: '복수하다' feels like paying someone back, but '설욕하다' is about winning a rematch or contest to restore your honor. It often appears in sports news in the phrase '패배를 설욕하다'.

en: to be terrified; to be frightened

examples.en: A sudden sound on the night road gave me chills.
The last scene of that movie is chilling.
I got a creepy feeling and looked behind me.
I felt a chill after watching the news.
When a cold hand touched me, a chill ran down my back.
The creepily smiling doll is scary.

explain: '무섭다'보다 갑자기 소름이 끼치는 느낌이에요. 소리, 장면, 이야기에 대해 '섬뜩한 느낌/기분'이 든다고 자주 말해요. '오싹하다'는 추위나 공포에 몸이 떨리는 느낌이고, '섬뜩하다'는 마음이 서늘해지는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 뒤에서 누가 보는 것 같아서 섬뜩한 느낌이 들었어요.
phrases.en: I felt creeped out as if someone was watching from behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '섬뜩한'으로 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it becomes 섬뜩한.

phrases.en: This story is not very chilling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 무섭지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says it is not scary.

phrases.en: I get chills hearing the ghost story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 떨리는 느낌이 있다는 점이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: It differs in that your body shivers.

explain_en: It is the feeling of sudden goosebumps, more than plain '무섭다'. People often say '섬뜩한 느낌' or '섬뜩한 기분' about a sound, a scene or a story. '오싹하다' is a shudder from cold or fear in the body, while '섬뜩하다' is a chill in the mind.

examples.en: If you envy a friend's success, only your own heart suffers.

examples.ko: 동료가 상을 받자 몇몇 사람이 시기했어요.
examples.en: When a colleague won a prize, a few people grew envious.
There are more people envious of him than you'd think.

examples.ko: 남을 시기해서 좋을 일은 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: Nothing good comes from envying others.

examples.ko: 시기한 나머지 그에게 말도 걸지 않았어요.
examples.en: Out of jealousy, I didn't even speak to him.
Don't be jealous of your sibling; help each other.

explain: '부러워하다'는 좋은 뜻으로도 쓰지만 '시기하다'는 남이 잘되는 것을 못마땅해하는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. '질투하다'는 연인이나 친구 관계에 많이 쓰고, '시기하다'는 성공·재능·지위 같은 일에 써요. 시간을 뜻하는 '시기'와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I felt envious of my friend, and it was hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시기하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾸면 남이 잘되는 것을 못마땅해하는 마음을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form names the resentful feeling you have when someone else does well.

phrases.en: Don't envy other people's success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부탁하거나 충고할 때 쓰는 부정 명령 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request form used to advise someone.

phrases.example: 몇몇 사람이 그의 재능을 시기하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Some people are envious of his talent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 그런 마음을 갖고 있다는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a jealous feeling that someone holds right now.

explain_en: '부러워하다' can be positive, but '시기하다' carries a bad feeling of resenting someone else's good fortune. '질투하다' is common for lovers or friends, while '시기하다' is for success, talent, or status. It is a different word from '시기' meaning a period of time.

en: to be mentally ill; to go insane

examples.ko: 혼자 웃고 있으면 사람들이 실성했다고 생각해요.
examples.en: If you laugh alone, people think you've lost it.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 그녀는 실성한 사람처럼 울었어요.
examples.en: Hearing the news, she cried like someone who had lost her mind.

examples.ko: 아이를 잃어버리면 엄마가 실성할 정도로 놀라요.
examples.en: If a mother loses her child, she is frightened to the point of losing her mind.

examples.ko: 너무 슬퍼서 실성해 버릴 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I was so sad that I felt I would go out of my mind.
Singing in the middle of the night, he must have lost it.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 실성하지 않고 버틴 게 대단해요.
examples.en: It's amazing that he held on without losing his mind.

explain: '실성한 사람처럼'은 너무 놀라거나 슬퍼서 정신이 나간 듯한 모습을 비유로 많이 말해요. 친구끼리 가볍게 '너 실성했어?'라고 하기도 하지만 실제 병을 가리킬 때는 상처가 될 수 있어서 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 복권에 당첨되자 그는 실성한 사람처럼 웃었어요.
phrases.en: When he won the lottery, he laughed like a madman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정신이 나간 듯 행동하는 모습을 비유할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to compare someone's behavior to losing their senses.
phrases.en_equiv: like someone who has lost it

phrases.example: 혼자 막 웃길래 '너 실성했어?' 하고 물어봤어요.
phrases.en: He was laughing by himself, so I asked, 'Have you lost it?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리 놀리듯이 쓰는 반말이지만 말투에 따라 기분 나쁠 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to tease a friend, but it can sound hurtful depending on the tone.

phrases.example: 소식을 듣고 그녀는 실성한 듯 울기만 했어요.
phrases.en: After hearing the news, she just cried as if she had lost her mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 듯'을 붙여 정신이 나간 것처럼 보이는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -ㄴ 듯 describes actions that look as if the person has lost their senses.
phrases.en_equiv: to cry as if out of one's mind

explain_en: '실성한 사람처럼' is often a comparison for someone who seems out of their mind from shock or grief. Friends may say '너 실성했어?' lightly, but it can hurt when it refers to a real illness, so be careful.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 뒤 그는 실의에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, he fell into despair.

examples.ko: 실의에 잠겨 있던 친구가 오늘 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend, who had been sunk in dejection, smiled today.

examples.ko: 실의에 빠진 사람에게는 따뜻한 말 한마디가 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: A warm word can be a great help to someone in despair.

examples.ko: 실의를 딛고 다시 일어서는 모습이 멋있었어요.
examples.en: It was impressive to see him rise again, overcoming his despair.

examples.ko: 저는 실의에 찬 얼굴로 집에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I came home with a face full of dejection.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 실의에 빠져 있다가 새 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: After being in low spirits for a long time, I started a new job.

explain: 일이 뜻대로 안 돼서 의욕을 잃은 마음을 말하고, 거의 '실의에 빠지다/잠기다/차다'처럼 정해진 짝으로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '풀이 죽다', '의욕이 없다'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, '실의'는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: When his business failed, he fell into despair.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실의'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 정해진 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common fixed pairing with 실의.

phrases.example: 그녀는 실의를 딛고 일어서서 다시 도전했어요.
phrases.en: She overcame her despair and stood up to try again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 마음을 이겨 내고 다시 시작한다는 좋은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used positively for overcoming a low mood and starting again.

phrases.example: 시험을 망치고 동생이 풀이 죽어 있어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is downcast after botching the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실의'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression used much more often in daily conversation than 실의.

explain_en: It describes the feeling of losing motivation when things do not go your way, and it is almost always used in fixed pairings like '실의에 빠지다/잠기다/차다'. In everyday talk people often say '풀이 죽다' or '의욕이 없다', while '실의' appears more in writing and the news.

examples.ko: 사람들은 처음 그들의 초라하기 짝이 없는 행색을 보고 아연실색했어요.
examples.en: People were aghast when they first saw how shabby they looked.
I was stunned when I saw the expensive price tag.
The whole family was dumbstruck by the sudden news.

examples.ko: 아연실색한 얼굴로 그는 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: With a stunned face, he couldn't say a word.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 거짓말을 했다는 걸 알고 다들 아연실색했어요.
examples.en: Everyone was appalled to learn that he had lied.

examples.ko: 집이 엉망인 걸 보고 아연실색하지 않을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't help but be aghast at seeing the house in a mess.

explain: '깜짝 놀라다'보다 훨씬 크게 충격을 받아 말문이 막힐 때 써요. 기쁜 놀람보다는 황당하거나 어이없는 일에 어울려요. 말할 때보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The customer who saw the price tag looked stunned.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'으로 활용해 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -한 form lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이런 결과가 나오다니 정말 아연실색할 일이에요.
phrases.en: Getting a result like this is truly shocking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 충격받을 만한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that would cause great shock.

phrases.en: I was so shocked that I was left speechless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬운 말로 비슷한 상황을 말할 수 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase for a similar situation.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '깜짝 놀라다': you are so shocked that you are left speechless. It fits dismaying or absurd events more than happy surprises. You see it more in writing and news than in casual speech.

examples.en: A sense of relief washed over me when the exam ended.
I felt relieved at the news that the child was safe.
I feel secure when my family is by my side.
Hearing his voice gave me a sense of relief.

examples.ko: 큰 걱정이 사라져서 안도감에 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: My big worry disappeared, and I cried from relief.
This room strangely makes me feel at ease.

explain: '안도감을 느끼다/주다', '안도감이 들다'로 써요. 말로는 '다행이다', '마음이 놓이다'가 더 자주 나오고, '안도감'은 글이나 설명할 때 잘 써요. 반대로 불안한 마음은 '불안감'이에요.

phrases.en: I felt relieved when I got home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 놓이는 느낌이 저절로 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a feeling of relief arises on its own.

phrases.en: My teacher's words gave me a sense of relief.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이나 말이 마음을 놓이게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person or words make someone feel at ease.

phrases.en: I felt at ease after hearing the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안도감과 비슷한 뜻이고, 말할 때는 이 표현이 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 안도감, and more common in speech.

explain_en: You say '안도감을 느끼다/주다' and '안도감이 들다'. In speech, '다행이다' and '마음이 놓이다' are more common; '안도감' fits writing and explanations better. The opposite feeling is '불안감'.

en: to be fidgety; to be screwed up; to be on thorns

examples.en: I was restless while waiting for the exam results.
My parents are on edge because the child is late.
Why are you so fidgety?
I was so restless before the interview that I only drank water.

examples.ko: 그는 안절부절못하는 모습으로 방 안을 서성였어요.
examples.en: He paced around the room looking anxious and restless.
I'm anxious in case my secret gets found out.

explain: 불안하거나 초조해서 가만히 있지 못하고 서성이는 모습을 말해요. 표준어는 '안절부절못하다'이고 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '안절부절못하는 모습'처럼 뒤에서 꾸미는 말로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: His restless look was noticeable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach a noun after it to describe someone's look.

phrases.en: He paced back and forth at the door, unable to settle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불안한 몸짓을 구체적으로 이어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a concrete action showing the anxiety.

phrases.en: I waited anxiously for the results to be announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 초조하게 기다리는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '-며' to describe waiting in a restless, anxious state.

explain_en: It describes being so anxious or nervous that you cannot stay still and keep pacing or fidgeting. The standard form is '안절부절못하다', written as one word. It is also commonly used before a noun, as in '안절부절못하는 모습'.

examples.en: I shivered at the cold that suddenly swept over me.
Anxiety crept over me as I walked along the night road.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 두려움이 엄습해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Fear hit me the night before the exam, and I couldn't sleep.
If fatigue suddenly hits you, take a short break.
On the morning the cold wave struck, the city froze over.
Terror overwhelmed me when I heard the news.

explain: 추위, 두려움, 불안, 피로, 졸음처럼 막을 수 없는 것이 갑자기 몰려올 때 써요. 주로 감정이나 느낌, 날씨가 주어가 돼요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 몰려오다'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 집에 오는 길에 피곤함이 엄습해 왔어요.
phrases.en: On my way home, exhaustion suddenly came over me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄습하다'에 '-아 오다'를 붙여 무언가가 다가오는 느낌을 살려요. 피로나 두려움에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아 오다' conveys something closing in on you, often fatigue or fear.

phrases.en: When I entered the dark alley, fear struck me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 주어일 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 갑자기 두려워지는 순간에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with an emotion as the subject, for a sudden rush of fear.

phrases.example: 점심을 먹고 나니 졸음이 확 몰려와요.
phrases.en: After lunch, sleepiness hits me all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄습하다'보다 쉬운 일상 말투예요. 대화에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday way to say it in conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to rush over all at once

explain_en: Use it when something you cannot stop, like cold, fear, anxiety, fatigue or sleepiness, suddenly rushes over you. The subject is usually a feeling, sensation or weather. In casual talk people may say '확 몰려오다' instead.

examples.en: Before I knew it, I had said 'yes'.
I was startled and screamed without thinking.
On instinct, I grabbed my friend's hand and ran.
In my confusion, I ended up handing over my wallet.
My name was called suddenly, and I stood up without thinking.
I said it on the spur of the moment, so I regret it now.

explain: 거의 '엉겁결에' 모양으로만 써요. 놀라거나 당황해서 생각할 틈 없이 한 행동에 쓰고, 별 생각 없이 한 행동에 쓰는 '무심코'와는 당황한 느낌이 있다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: My friend laughed, so I did it too without thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각할 틈 없이 다른 사람의 행동을 따라 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you copy someone's action without time to think.

phrases.example: 사람이 많아서 엉겁결에 친구 손을 잡았어요.
phrases.en: It was crowded, so I grabbed my friend's hand on impulse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 당황해서 나온 몸의 행동에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits physical actions that come from surprise or panic.
phrases.en_equiv: to grab a hand on reflex

phrases.en: I blurted out the secret without meaning to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당황해서 말이 먼저 나왔다는 후회의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a sense of regret that the words slipped out in a panic.

explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '엉겁결에'. It fits actions done without time to think because you were surprised or flustered, which differs from '무심코' (without really thinking), which has no sense of panic.

examples.ko: 영웅심에 위험한 일에 뛰어들면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't jump into dangerous things out of a hero complex.
That friend has too strong a desire to be a hero.

examples.ko: 영웅심 때문에 혼자 일을 다 맡았어요.
examples.en: Because of my hero complex, I took on all the work alone.
It was an act that came from a small streak of wanting to be a hero.
The child tried to help his friend out of a wish to be a hero.

examples.ko: 괜한 영웅심을 부리다가 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: You could get hurt showing off an unnecessary hero act.

explain: 남 앞에서 멋지게 나서고 싶은 마음을 말해요. '영웅심을 부리다', '영웅심에 ~하다'처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 조금 무모하다는 느낌이 들어갈 때가 많아요. '영웅심리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: You can get hurt if you show off like a hero.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멋지게 나서고 싶은 마음을 겉으로 드러낸다는 뜻이고 조금 무모하다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means showing off the wish to look heroic, with a hint of recklessness.

phrases.en: My urge to be a hero came first, so I tried to solve it alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 생각보다 멋지게 나서려는 마음이 먼저일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the wish to look heroic outweighs other thoughts.

phrases.en: That behavior is because of a hero complex.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영웅심'과 거의 같은 뜻으로, 행동의 이유를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '영웅심', used to explain the reason for a behavior.

explain_en: It refers to the urge to step forward and look impressive in front of others. It is often used as '영웅심을 부리다' or '영웅심에 ~하다', frequently with a hint of recklessness. People also say '영웅심리'.

examples.en: Strength surges up in my chest.
Hot water gushed up from underground.
Joy welled up at the news of the victory.
Spring water gushes out from between the rocks.
Starting a new job makes my motivation surge.
Anger surged up so much that I couldn't speak.

explain: 물이 솟는 모습뿐 아니라 힘, 기쁨, 의욕 같은 마음이 크게 솟아오를 때도 많이 써요. '솟구치다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있지만 '용솟음치다'가 조금 더 글에서 자주 보여요. 활용은 '용솟음쳐요', '용솟음쳤어요'예요.

phrases.en: Joy surges up in my chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '솟구치다'는 '용솟음치다'와 비슷한데 말할 때도 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '솟구치다' is close in meaning but is used more often in speech.

phrases.en: I could not hide the joy welling up inside me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 감정이 크게 솟을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used before a noun for strongly rising feelings.

phrases.en: Clear water is gushing out of the spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 솟아 나오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that is gushing out right now.

explain_en: It describes not only water spurting up but also strong feelings such as strength, joy or motivation surging. It is close to '솟구치다' but appears a bit more in writing. It conjugates as '용솟음쳐요' and '용솟음쳤어요'.

examples.en: I lost my temper the moment I heard it and shouted.

examples.ko: 욱하는 성격 때문에 후회할 말을 할 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Because I have a short temper, I often say things I regret.
I flared up for a moment, but I took a deep breath and held back.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 욱하면 아무 말도 안 들려요.
examples.en: When he flares up, he can't hear anything anyone says.

examples.ko: 욱하지 말고 일단 차분히 얘기해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't lose your temper; let's talk calmly first.

examples.ko: 욱한 마음에 보낸 문자를 바로 지웠어요.
examples.en: I deleted the text I sent in a fit of anger right away.

explain: 갑자기 화가 확 치밀 때 써요. 오래 화나 있는 게 아니라 순간적으로 폭발하는 느낌이라서 '화나다'와 달라요. 겉으로 터뜨리는 '욱하다'와 속으로 오래 담아 두는 '꽁하다'는 반대 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 화나도 욱하지 말고 먼저 말해 보세요.
phrases.en: Even if you're angry, don't flare up; talk first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순간적으로 화내지 말라고 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone not to explode in anger.

phrases.en: In a burst of anger, I slammed the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 화가 나서 한 행동의 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the reason for something done in a sudden burst of anger.

phrases.en: I told my friend, 'Sorry, I lost my temper for a moment.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 사과할 때 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used to apologize to a close friend.

explain_en: Used when anger suddenly surges up. It is a short burst, not lasting anger, which makes it different from '화나다'. '욱하다' (exploding outwardly) and '꽁하다' (holding it in for a long time) feel like opposites.

examples.en: The child suddenly burst into tears.
The moment I saw Mom's face, I burst out crying.

examples.ko: 동생은 울음보가 한번 터지면 잘 안 그쳐요.
examples.en: Once my younger sibling starts crying, it's hard to stop.
At my friend's comfort, I burst into the tears I had been holding back.

examples.ko: 울음보는 한 번 터지면 막기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once the tears start flowing, they are hard to stop.
My face turned red from holding back my tears.

explain: 울음이 가득 들어 있는 주머니처럼 보는 말이라 거의 '터지다', '터뜨리다'와 함께 써요. 아이나 감정이 북받친 사람이 갑자기 크게 울 때 잘 어울려요. 단독으로 말하기보다 굳은 짝말로 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 시상식에서 그 선수는 결국 울음보를 터뜨렸어요.
phrases.en: to burst into tears
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 울음을 한꺼번에 크게 쏟아낼 때 써요. 조용히 눈물이 나는 것과는 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when held-back crying comes out all at once and loudly, unlike quietly shedding tears.

explain_en: It treats crying as something stored in a pouch, so it almost always goes with '터지다' or '터뜨리다'. It suits a child or an emotional person suddenly crying hard. Learn it as a fixed collocation rather than on its own.

examples.ko: 어머니 목소리를 들으니 울컥 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Hearing my mother's voice, I suddenly teared up.

examples.ko: 친구 말을 듣다가 울컥 화가 치밀었어요.
examples.en: While listening to my friend, anger suddenly surged up.

examples.ko: 감동적인 영상을 보고 울컥 목이 메었어요.
examples.en: Watching the moving video, my throat suddenly tightened.

examples.ko: 마음이 울컥 올라와서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: Emotion welled up so suddenly that I couldn't speak.
My stomach lurched on the bus, so I got off in a hurry.
When I hear the graduation song, my chest tightens with emotion.

explain: 슬픔, 감동, 화가 갑자기 올라올 때 써요. '울컥 눈물이 나다', '울컥 화가 나다'처럼 말해요. 서서히 쌓이는 감정에는 안 맞고 순간적으로 확 올라오는 느낌이에요. 속이 메스꺼울 때 '울컥 올라오다'도 써요.

phrases.en: As soon as I got in the car, my stomach suddenly heaved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메스꺼워서 갑자기 올라오는 느낌에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a sudden rising feeling of nausea.

phrases.en: I suddenly flared up in anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참다가 순간적으로 화가 확 나는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Anger that flashes up suddenly after holding it in.

phrases.en: While watching the movie, I suddenly felt like crying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감동이나 슬픔 때문에 울음이 갑자기 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For tears coming suddenly from emotion or sadness.

explain_en: It is for sadness, being moved, or anger that surges up suddenly, as in '울컥 눈물이 나다' and '울컥 화가 나다'. It does not fit feelings that build slowly. It is also used when nausea rises, as in '울컥 올라오다'.

examples.ko: 실수를 해서 친구들 사이에서 웃음거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: I made a mistake and became a laughingstock among my friends.
I don't like becoming a laughingstock.
His strange clothes were a joke for a while.

examples.ko: 이 이야기는 두고두고 웃음거리로 남을 거예요.
examples.en: This story will remain something to laugh about for a long time.
I made a joke on purpose to ease the mood.
You must not make someone a laughingstock.

explain: '웃음거리'는 보통 '웃음거리가 되다', '웃음거리로 만들다'처럼 써요. 대부분 놀림의 뜻이 있어서 기분 나쁜 상황에 어울려요. 즐겁게 웃는 이야기는 '우스운 이야기'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 사람들 앞에서 친구를 웃음거리로 만들면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't make your friend a laughingstock in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 놀림받게 할 때 써요. 대부분 나쁜 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making someone an object of ridicule. It usually describes bad behavior.

phrases.example: 저는 발표에서 실수해서 웃음거리가 되고 싶지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't want to be laughed at for making a mistake in my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶지 않다'로 걱정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -고 싶지 않다 to express worry.
phrases.en_equiv: I don't want to be a laughingstock

phrases.example: 그 별명이 친구들 사이에서 놀림거리가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That nickname became something to tease about among friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃음거리'와 비슷하지만 놀리는 마음이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 웃음거리 but the teasing intent is clearer.

explain_en: '웃음거리' is usually said as '웃음거리가 되다' or '웃음거리로 만들다'. It mostly carries a mocking tone, so it fits unpleasant situations. A pleasantly funny story is a '우스운 이야기'.

en: to be resentful; to be reproachful

examples.ko: 그 사람이 원망스러워서 말도 하기 싫어요.
examples.en: I resent him so much that I do not even want to talk.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지니 공부 안 한 내가 원망스러웠어요.
examples.en: After failing the test, I blamed myself for not studying.

examples.ko: 약속을 어긴 친구가 원망스럽지만 이해도 돼요.
examples.en: I resent my friend who broke the promise, but I understand too.
He looked at me with reproachful eyes.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 소풍을 못 가니 날씨가 원망스러워요.
examples.en: We cannot go on the picnic because of rain, so I resent the weather.
Nobody helped me, so I felt bitter toward the world.

explain: 기대했는데 서운해서 탓하고 싶은 마음이에요. 실망한 느낌이 들어 있어요. 사람이 아닌 날씨나 세상에도 쓸 수 있어요. 탓하는 행동은 동사 '원망하다'예요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looked at me with a resentful look.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에 쓰고, 서운한 마음이 보이는 눈빛을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies a noun, describing eyes that show hurt, reproachful feelings.

phrases.example: 시간이 지나서 이제 그 일이 원망스럽지 않아요.
phrases.en: Time has passed, so I no longer resent that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 풀렸을 때 '원망스럽지 않다'라고 부정으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when the resentful feeling has faded.

phrases.en: With hard times continuing, I felt resentful toward the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아닌 세상이나 운에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can also be used for things that are not people, such as the world or fate.

explain_en: The feeling of wanting to blame someone because you hoped for more and were let down. It carries disappointment, and can be aimed at things like the weather or the world. The action of blaming is the verb '원망하다'.

examples.en: As the economy worsened, employees' sense of crisis grew.

examples.ko: 저는 시험 전날이 되자 위기감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: On the day before the exam, I felt a sense of crisis.

examples.ko: 회사는 위기감 속에서 새 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The company made a new plan amid a sense of crisis.
A sense of crisis sometimes gets people moving.
Driven by a sense of crisis, I studied all night.
That sense of crisis made the team stronger.

explain: '-감'이 붙으면 상황이 아니라 그 느낌을 말해요. '위기'는 위험한 상황이고 '위기감'은 그 느낌이에요. '위기감을 느끼다', '위기감이 커지다'처럼 쓰고, '긴장감', '불안감'도 같은 방식이에요.

phrases.en: My sense of crisis grew after watching the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위기감이 커지다'와 비슷해요. 불안한 느낌이 점점 강해진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '위기감이 커지다'. The feeling of danger gets stronger.

phrases.en: That team has no sense of crisis, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 상황인데도 별로 걱정하지 않는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone isn't worried even though the situation is risky.

phrases.example: 새 경쟁 회사가 우리에게 위기감을 줬어요.
phrases.en: The new rival company gave us a sense of crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이나 사람이 불안한 느낌을 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something or someone creates a feeling of danger.
phrases.en_equiv: to create a sense of crisis

explain_en: Adding -감 turns a situation into the feeling about it. 위기 is the dangerous situation, and 위기감 is the feeling of it. It goes with 위기감을 느끼다 and 위기감이 커지다, and 긴장감 and 불안감 work the same way.

examples.en: I was so angry that I ground my teeth.
I crunched down on a hard candy.

examples.ko: 얼음을 으드득 씹어 먹으면 이에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Crunching on ice is bad for your teeth.

examples.ko: 자는 동안 으드득 소리가 나서 잠에서 깼어요.
examples.en: A grinding sound woke me up while I was sleeping.

examples.ko: 으드득 소리가 날 만큼 세게 깨물었어요.
examples.en: I bit down so hard that it made a crunching sound.

examples.ko: 그는 으드득 소리를 내며 이를 악물었어요.
examples.en: He clenched his teeth with a grinding sound.

explain: 단단한 것을 힘주어 깨물거나 이를 갈 때 나는 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. 눈을 밟는 소리는 보통 '뽀드득'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I chewed the ice with a crunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱한 음식을 힘주어 씹는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sound of chewing something hard with force.

phrases.example: 딱딱한 과자를 먹을 때 으드득 소리가 났어요.
phrases.en: A crunching sound came out when I ate the hard cookie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 것이 부서지거나 갈릴 때 나는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the sound when something hard breaks or grinds.

phrases.example: 자는 동안 이를 으드득 가는 버릇이 있어요.
phrases.en: I have a habit of grinding my teeth while I sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 '이를 으드득 갈다'로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mostly used in the set phrase 이를 으드득 갈다.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of biting hard on something firm or grinding your teeth. The sound of stepping on snow is usually '뽀드득' instead.

examples.en: His sudden words made me wonder.
I couldn't hide my puzzlement and asked back.

examples.ko: 아무도 없는데 소리가 나서 의아심이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A sound came though nobody was there, and it puzzled me.
My friend looked at me with a face full of puzzlement.
Puzzled, I asked him directly.
I looked up several things to clear up my doubts.

explain: '의아심이 들다/생기다', '의아심을 품다'처럼 써요. '의심'은 믿지 못하는 느낌이고, '의아심'은 이상해서 고개를 갸웃하는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '이상하다', '왜 그러지?'라고 말하는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: I felt puzzled after hearing those words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 이상하게 느껴질 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural collocation when something suddenly seems strange.

phrases.en: I had doubts about his answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '품다'는 마음속에 계속 가지고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 품다 suggests keeping the feeling in one's mind.

phrases.en: My friend looked at me with a puzzled expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '의아하다'를 써서 얼굴 표정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the adjective 의아하다 to describe a facial expression.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like '의아심이 들다/생기다' and '의아심을 품다'. '의심' is not believing something, while '의아심' is the puzzled feeling of finding something strange. In daily talk people often just say '이상하다' or '왜 그러지?'.

examples.en: If you fall into conceit, it's easy to make mistakes.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 자만심을 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't get conceited just because you won once.
His arrogance damaged the teamwork.
Conceit gets in the way of growth.
Because of my conceit, I ignored the advice.
I want to learn humility instead of conceit.

explain: '자신감'은 좋은 뜻이지만 '자만심'은 자기가 잘났다고 지나치게 믿는 마음이라 나쁘게 들려요. 반대말은 '겸손'이고, 같은 뜻의 동사는 '자만하다'예요.

phrases.en: Don't get conceited just because you succeeded.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자만심'과 같은 말에서 나온 동사이고, 행동이나 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used to talk about attitude or behavior.

phrases.example: 자만심이 강한 사람은 조언을 잘 안 들어요.
phrases.en: A person with strong conceit rarely listens to advice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 잘났다는 믿음이 크다는 뜻이고 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a strong belief in one's own superiority, negatively.

phrases.en: I put aside my conceit and learn humbly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겸손'과 같이 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with 'humility'.

explain_en: '자신감' (confidence) is positive, but '자만심' is an excessive belief that you are great, so it sounds negative. The opposite is '겸손' (humility), and the related verb is '자만하다'.
